restDay.label: Rest day
restDay.headline: Not a day off — a day the muscle actually grows.
restDay.note: Growth happens between sessions, not during them. Walking is fine and good. Everything else on this list still counts, so a rest day never breaks the streak.

home.label: Bodyweight
home.note: No equipment. Progression is by variation and tempo instead of weight: when you hit the top of the rep range on every set, move up a rung and drop back to the bottom of the range.

sessions.label: Upper — Push
sessions.headline: Chest and triceps. Pike push-ups are the closest thing to shoulder work you have.

items.detail: Elbows about 45° from your body, not flared. Full range — chest to the floor.

alternatives.detail: Hands set wider than shoulders, elbows flare a little more than usual. Shifts more of the load onto the chest.
As you lower, bring one knee toward the same-side elbow, alternating sides each rep. Chest and triceps with a bit of core.
One hand set a fist-length ahead of the other, elbows tucked. Loads the rear arm harder — swap the lead hand each set.

items.detail: Hips high, head travels toward the floor between your hands. The best delt work available without weights — treat it as the priority movement of this session.

alternatives.detail: Feet against the wall, walk them up while walking your hands back until you're near vertical, then reverse it. Builds the pressing strength pike work is training toward.
Hold the top pike position and tap the opposite shoulder without letting your hips sway. Delts and core, no press required.
From a pike, dive forward and down, sweep through to a cobra, then reverse back to pike. Shoulders, chest and triceps in one flowing rep.

items.detail: Two stable chairs or the edge of a sofa. Shoulders down, don't sink into the shrug.

alternatives.detail: Sit with knees bent, hands on the floor beside your hips, lift your hips and bend the elbows straight back. Same dip pattern, no furniture — just less range.
Hands under your shoulders, elbows tucked tight to your ribs as you lower. Zero setup, still triceps-dominant.
One sturdy step or a single chair instead of two. Same movement, half the furniture.

items.detail: Hands together under the chest. Triceps.

alternatives.detail: Kneeling, hands a little ahead of your knees, body in a straight line to your head. Bend only the elbows to lower your forehead toward the floor and press back — nearly pure triceps.
Hands by your ribs instead of your shoulders, lean your whole body forward over them before bending the elbows. Triceps and front delts at a steeper angle.
Push up quickly enough that your hands almost leave the floor, land soft, reset. Trains the same triceps as the diamond, just for power instead of grind.

items.detail: Reps per set, and which rung you're on. Without it, next session has nothing to beat.

sessions.label: Core & Back
sessions.headline: Trunk and mid-back. Two leg moves at the end so they don't vanish entirely.

ladder: Reverse snow angel, paused at the top
items.detail: Face down, arms out on the floor, palms up. Sweep them from beside your hips up over your head and back, keeping hands lifted the whole time. Burns the mid-back and rear delts.

alternatives.detail: Back, head and arms against a wall, slide your arms from a W up to a Y overhead and back down without losing contact. Rear delts and lower traps, standing instead of on the floor.
Lying face down like superman, pull your elbows back past your ribs as you lift your chest higher — rowing while flying. Mid-back and rear delts together.
Face down, sweep your arms through a Y, then a T, then a W, pausing briefly in each. Hits the rear delts from three angles in one set.

items.detail: Lower back pressed flat into the floor the whole time.

alternatives.detail: On your back, arms reaching up, knees bent at 90°. Lower one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor without your lower back arching, then reset.
Lie flat, then fold at the hips to bring straight legs and arms up to meet over your middle, lower with control. A moving version of the same hollow-body shape.
On your back, knees pulled to your chest, curl your hips off the floor in a small lift and lower without your feet touching down. Lower abs, kept under constant tension.
Hands and toes on the floor, knees hovering an inch up, back flat. Same brace as the plank, hips a little higher, quads working too.
Plank position, drive one knee toward your chest at a time, controlled rather than fast. Core with a bit more heart rate.
On hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg straight out and hold, then switch without your hips rocking. Core stability, easier on the wrists than a plank.

items.detail: Builds the waist taper from the side.

alternatives.detail: On your back, knees bent and lifted, rock them side to side while keeping your shoulders flat on the floor. Obliques, moving instead of held.
Standing, hand behind your head, lift the same-side knee while crunching your elbow down toward it. Obliques, no floor needed.
From a side plank, dip your hips toward the floor and lift back up instead of holding still. Same muscles, worked through a range.

items.detail: Lower back and spinal erectors.

alternatives.detail: Same superman position, but lift and lower a couple of inches for reps instead of holding still. Same lower-back work, through a small range.
Standing, soft knees, hinge forward at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, then hold. Same lower-back work, standing instead of on the floor.
Face down, lift opposite arm and leg together for a couple of seconds, lower, then switch sides. Same erector work, moving instead of static.

items.detail: Legs kept ticking over, not the focus any more.

alternatives.detail: Step one leg back, drop the rear knee toward the floor, push back to standing. Same quads and glutes, one leg at a time.
On your back, knees bent, drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line, squeeze at the top. Glutes and hamstrings, easier on the knees.
Back against a wall, thighs parallel to the floor, hold. Same quads as the squat, held instead of repped.

ladder: Single-leg calf raise off a step

alternatives.detail: Sit, hands pressing down on your knees for a little extra resistance, raise your heels as high as you can. Bent-knee calf work — a different part of the calf than the standing version.
Walk in place on your toes, heels never touching down. Same calves, continuous tension instead of discrete reps.
Hinge forward slightly, hands resting on a wall or your own thighs, raise your heels. A different angle on the same calf muscles.

sessions.label: Upper — Pull
sessions.headline: The hardest session to do without a bar. Inverted rows are the whole game here.

items.detail: Grip one hand with the other in front of your chest. Pull the working arm back into a row while the other hand fights it. Push hard — you only get out what you put in.

alternatives.detail: Face down, arms out on the floor, palms up, sweep them overhead and back. Mid-back and rear delts, no arm-against-arm tension needed.
Sit under a sturdy table, grip the edge, feet braced, pull your chest up toward it. About as close as bodyweight gets to an actual loaded row.
Lying face down like superman, pull your elbows back past your ribs as you lift your chest higher — rowing while flying. Mid-back and rear delts together.

items.detail: Face down, arms and legs lifted, flutter opposite arm and leg. Lower back and the whole rear chain.

alternatives.detail: Sit with legs out, hands behind your hips, press up until your body forms a straight line facing the ceiling. Whole rear chain, from underneath instead of above.
On hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg straight out and hold, then switch without your hips rocking. Rear chain and balance, easier on the lower back than the swimmer.
On your back, hips lifted into a bridge, lift one foot off the floor at a time without dropping your hips. Glutes and lower back, held instead of fluttering.

items.detail: Face down, arms making a Y then T then W. Rear delts and mid-back — this is genuinely useful equipment-free work and it protects your shoulders for the gym later.

alternatives.detail: Back, head and arms against a wall, slide your arms from a W up to a Y overhead and back down without losing contact. Same rear-delt pattern as the Y-T-W, standing instead of prone.
Face down, arms out to your sides, draw small backward circles with straight arms. Same rear-delt endurance work, continuous instead of held positions.
Hinge forward at the hips, soft knees, sweep your arms out to the sides and squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower with control. Rear delts, standing and moving instead of prone and held.

items.detail: Lower back and spinal erectors.

alternatives.detail: Same superman position, but lift and lower a couple of inches for reps instead of holding still. Same lower-back work, through a small range.
Standing, soft knees, hinge forward at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, then hold. Same lower-back work, standing instead of on the floor.
Face down, lift opposite arm and leg together for a couple of seconds, lower, then switch sides. Same erector work, moving instead of static.

sessions.label: Arms & shoulders
sessions.headline: Second shoulder exposure of the week. Do these when you're fresh, not tacked on tired.

items.detail: Second exposure this week. Frequency is what you have instead of load.

alternatives.detail: Feet against the wall, walk them up while walking your hands back until you're near vertical, then reverse it. Builds the pressing strength pike work is training toward.
Hold the top pike position and tap the opposite shoulder without letting your hips sway. Delts and core, no press required.
From a pike, dive forward and down, sweep through to a cobra, then reverse back to pike. Shoulders, chest and triceps in one flowing rep.

items.detail: Triceps.

alternatives.detail: Sit with knees bent, hands on the floor beside your hips, lift your hips and bend the elbows straight back. Same dip pattern, no furniture — just less range.
Hands under your shoulders, elbows tucked tight to your ribs as you lower. Zero setup, still triceps-dominant.
One sturdy step or a single chair instead of two. Same movement, half the furniture.
Kneeling, hands a little ahead of your knees, body in a straight line to your head. Bend only the elbows to lower your forehead toward the floor and press back — nearly pure triceps.
Hands by your ribs instead of your shoulders, lean your whole body forward over them before bending the elbows. Triceps and front delts at a steeper angle.
Push up quickly enough that your hands almost leave the floor, land soft, reset. Trains the same triceps as the diamond, just for power instead of grind.

items.detail: Rear and medial delts. Slow — there's no weight, so time under tension is all you've got.

alternatives.detail: Back, head and arms against a wall, slide your arms from a W up to a Y overhead and back down without losing contact. Same rear-delt pattern as the Y raise, with the wall giving you feedback on form.
Face down, arms out on the floor, palms up, sweep them overhead and back. Rear delts and mid-back, moving through a full range instead of held at the top.
Face down, arms out to your sides, draw small backward circles with straight arms. Same rear-delt endurance work, continuous instead of a discrete raise.

items.detail: Stand side-on, press the back of your hand into the wall as if raising the arm, and hold. Being straight with you: this is a poor substitute for a loaded lateral raise and won't build much width. It's here to keep the movement pattern alive until you have dumbbells.

alternatives.detail: Lie on your side, top arm straight, raise it until it's in line with your shoulder, then lower slowly. Real range of motion against gravity, not just a static push — probably your best lateral-delt option without weight.
Raise one arm out to the side; the other hand presses down on the wrist to resist it through the range. Same trick as the self-resistance row, aimed at the side delt.
Stand in a doorway, press the backs of both wrists outward into the frame at shoulder height, hold. Same isometric idea as the wall version, both sides at once.

gym.label: Gym
gym.note: Parked until you have a subscription. Switch by setting activeProgram to "gym" — nothing else needs rewriting.

sessions.label: Upper — Push
sessions.headline: Lateral raises are the priority movement of the whole plan.

items.detail: Barbell or dumbbell. Your priority press.
The single biggest visual driver. Slow, no swinging.

sessions.label: Lower
sessions.headline: Keep it honest but don't let it eat your upper-body recovery.

items.detail: Barbell or hack.

sessions.label: Upper — Pull
sessions.headline: Back width is the other half of the V-taper.

items.detail: Back width = V-taper.

items.text: Lateral raise, machine or leaning cable · 4×12–15
items.detail: Yes, again. Different angle.
Shoulder health and width.

sessions.label: Arms & delts
sessions.headline: The weak-point day. Third lateral raise exposure of the week.

items.detail: As prescribed.
As prescribed. Consistent time of day.

daily.title: Eat
daily.note: Protein is the non-negotiable — 1.8–2.2 g per kg per day. Four anchors of 35–45 g beats trying to rescue the number at dinner. The failure mode isn't one light day, it's three in a row.

items.detail: Greek yoghurt or skyr + eggs, or a shake with milk.
Palm-and-a-half of chicken / fish / beef / tofu.
Whey shake or cottage cheese.
The one that usually rescues the day's total.
Pale straw, not clear. Creatine raises water needs slightly.
Only needed for the first 2–3 weeks, to calibrate. After that you'll know your portions by eye.
Any time of day. No loading phase needed.

daily.title: Care
daily.note: Minoxidil every evening, except on microneedling days — the skin needs about a day and a half to close up before anything goes on it again.

items.detail: Morning. Every 14 days. No minoxidil this evening — resume tomorrow evening.
Evening, on dry scalp. Hides itself automatically on microneedling days.
Short sleep measurably suppresses muscle gain and raises appetite. Consistent wake time matters more than consistent bedtime.
Tick it on the days you didn't. Worth tracking next to sleep — it changes sleep architecture, and sleep is the recovery lever the plan leans on hardest.
Not in the hour after training — cold blunts the growth signal.

oneOffs.title: Setup
oneOffs.note: These disappear for good once ticked.

items.detail: Morning, unflexed, before eating. This is the one thing here that gets worse by waiting — a starting number taken next week isn't a starting number.
As real appointments, not intentions. Mon / Tue / Thu / Fri.
Enough floor to lie flat with your arms out, and two chairs that take your weight for dips. That's the whole kit list.
